draft.title: The civil rights movement in the United States
card: Segregation was the legal separation of Black and white Americans in schools, buses and public places, mostly in the Southern states. Black citizens were also often stopped from voting.
Boycotts
People refused to use a service to put pressure on its owners. In the Montgomery bus boycott of 1955 to 1956, Black residents stayed off the city's buses for over a year.
Court cases
Lawyers argued that segregation broke the Constitution. In Brown v. Board of Education in 1954, the Supreme Court ruled that segregated public schools were unlawful.
Marches and laws
Marches such as Selma to Montgomery in 1965 drew national attention to the denial of voting rights. The Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 followed.
draft.remember: Boycotts, court cases and marches together pushed the United States to change its laws.

a.q: What was the main aim of the Montgomery bus boycott?
opts: To pressure the bus company into ending segregation
To make the Supreme Court rule on school segregation
To win the vote for Black citizens in Alabama
To pass a national law against discrimination in jobs
a.why: Black residents stopped riding the buses so the company lost income and faced pressure to end segregated seating. The school ruling in Brown v. Board of Education was a separate court case, not the aim of this boycott.
a.clue: A boycott works by refusing to use something.

b.q: In 1965 marchers walked from Selma to Montgomery, Alabama. Which problem were they mainly protesting about?
opts: Black citizens being blocked from voting
Black children being kept out of white schools
Black passengers being made to sit at the back of buses
Black workers being paid less than white workers
b.why: The Selma marches drew attention to the denial of voting rights, and the Voting Rights Act followed in 1965. School segregation is tempting, but that was the issue in Brown v. Board of Education in 1954, a court case rather than the Selma march.
b.clue: Think about which law followed the march in the same year.

a.best: To pressure the bus company into ending segregation

b.best: Black citizens being blocked from voting

Reword it, for example: 'Marches such as Washington in 1963 and Selma in 1965… The Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 followed', or tie only the Voting Rights Act to Selma.
